title: SSO provider throttling during scheduled key rollover leading to audit-event gaps and auth chain failures
creator: Ava Martínez
description: Follow-up for incident where our SSO provider entered a short-lived throttle window concurrent with a scheduled KMS-backed signing key rollover. Observed symptoms: failed token exchanges for customers behind SAML/IdP, 5xx spikes in our auth proxy, and gaps in downstream audit log ingestion in the 2025-02-17 02:10–02:28 UTC window. This ticket captures investigation notes, cross-team action items, and mitigations to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Approximately 12 customer tenants experienced login failures and API auth errors; audit ingestion for ~18k auth-related events was delayed and ~2.1k events were not captured in primary audit stream (later recovered from provider debug logs but missing upstream metadata). Business impact: elevated support volume, potential compliance exposure for regulated customers during window.
timeline: 2025-02-17T01:58:00Z - KMS key rotation job started (automated schedule).
2025-02-17T02:05:00Z - SSO provider reported slow token signing latency; internal metric alert triggered (auth-proxy-latency P90).
2025-02-17T02:10:00Z - External IdP began throttling token introspection calls per their rate-limiter (provider postmortem shows burst limit hit).
2025-02-17T02:12:00Z - Our auth-proxy started returning 502s for OIDC callbacks; rollback to cached signing key attempted but cache TTL had been invalidated by rotation.
2025-02-17T02:20:00Z - Audit-ingest service backpressure observed; queue length increased and retention window for streaming buffer approached overflow.
2025-02-17T02:28:00Z - SSO provider cleared throttling; KMS rotation completed. Normal traffic resumed.
2025-02-17T03:05:00Z - Post-incident triage begun; temporary mitigation implemented to rehydrate missing audit events from provider logs and publish to our long-term store.
root_cause_analysis: Primary: race between automated KMS signing-key rotation and peak token introspection traffic causing increased latency on provider side. The provider's burst-limiter rejected retries leading to auth failures.
Secondary: our auth-proxy aggressively invalidated local signing-key caches on rotation without a soft-grace period or fallback to previously-valid key for a short overlap.

Tertiary: audit-ingest streaming buffer had insufficient headroom for replays when downstream client calls retried, resulting in transient message drops that were not surfaced as 'critical' in alerting rules.
remediation_plan: Auth-proxy: implement key-rotation overlap semantics — hold previous signing key in cache for 15 minutes after rotation and accept tokens signed by previous key for that window. Owner: Owen Li. Due: 2025-03-09.

Rotation scheduling: add provider-aware coordination to KMS rotation job (query SSO provider throttle metrics API before initiating rotation; postpone if high traffic). Owner: Priya Kapoor (Infra SRE). Due: 2025-03-02.
Audit-ingest: increase streaming buffer watermark and add explicit soak tests that simulate bursts during rotation windows. Owner: Daniel Cho. Due: 2025-03-16.
Alerting: create an alert policy for 'audit-ingest drop rate' with paging for >0.1% drop over 5 minutes and add a dedicated runbook. Owner: Security Observability. Due: 2025-03-05.

Provider ops coordination: schedule quarterly SL vendor review and request a higher burst allowance or dedicated call lane for critical token-introspection paths. Owner: Vendor Management. Due: 2025-04-01.
Compliance: document recovered audit events and produce a customer-notification plan for impacted regulated tenants; legal & trust review required. Owner: Legal / Trust. Due: 2025-03-07.
Chaos tests: add an automated end-to-end scenario in staging that triggers key rotation during high auth traffic to validate graceful behavior. Owner: SRE. Due: 2025-03-23.
